body:
### What are you really trying to do?

Call `executeUpdateWithStart` in a resilient way — catching all errors with `.catch()` — without having Node.js terminate the process due to an `unhandledRejection`.

### Describe the bug

`executeUpdateWithStart` leaks a rejected Promise that the caller cannot reach with `.catch()` or `try/catch`. Node.js fires `unhandledRejection` and terminates the process in Node 15+, even though the caller's error handling is correct.

**Root cause** — `WithStartWorkflowOperation` creates `workflowHandlePromise` eagerly in its constructor with no `.catch()` handler ([`workflow-client.ts` lines 533–545, v1.15.0](https://github.com/temporalio/sdk-typescript/blob/v1.15.0/packages/client/src/workflow-client.ts#L533-L545)):

```ts
this.workflowHandlePromise = new Promise<WorkflowHandle<T>>((resolve, reject) => {
  this[withStartWorkflowOperationResolve] = resolve;
  this[withStartWorkflowOperationReject] = reject;
});
```

When `executeMultiOperation` fails at the gRPC transport level before any response is received (`seenStart === false`), `_updateWithStartHandler` does two things ([lines 1114–1128](https://github.com/temporalio/sdk-typescript/blob/v1.15.0/packages/client/src/workflow-client.ts#L1114-L1128)):

```ts
} catch (thrownError) {
  ...
  if (!seenStart) {
    onStartError(err); // ① rejects workflowHandlePromise — no handler attached
  }
  ...
  throw err;           // ② re-throws to caller
}
```

- **①** rejects `workflowHandlePromise`, which was never awaited and has no `.catch()`.
- **②** re-throws the same error to the caller, who catches it.

The caller handles ② correctly, but ① has already created an uncaught rejected Promise → `unhandledRejection` fires.

### Trigger condition

Any gRPC-level error from `executeMultiOperation` before the first response. The most reliable trigger: exceed `MaxConcurrentUpdatesPerWorkflow` (server default: 10). With no running worker, updates pile up as `ADMITTED`; the 11th concurrent call returns `RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED`, which takes the failing code path.

### Minimal Reproduction

Full self-contained reproduction (two files, runs in ~5 seconds):

**→ https://github.com/gioragutt/temporalio-update-with-start-unhandled-rejection**

```bash
git clone https://github.com/gioragutt/temporalio-update-with-start-unhandled-rejection
cd temporalio-update-with-start-unhandled-rejection
npm install
npm run reproduce
```

**Expected:**
```
Caught errors:        1
Unhandled rejections: 0
```

**Actual:**
```
UNHANDLED REJECTION: limit on number of concurrent in-flight updates has been reached (10)

Caught errors:        1
Unhandled rejections: 1

BUG REPRODUCED: unhandledRejection fired despite all errors being caught.
```

### Suggested fix

The SDK already uses this exact pattern in `packages/worker/src/activity.ts` (line 98) and `packages/worker/src/worker.ts` (line 640), and documents it in `packages/worker/src/errors.ts` (lines 18–20) as the canonical way to suppress unhandled rejections on intentionally-rejected internal promises.

```diff
 this.workflowHandlePromise = new Promise<WorkflowHandle<T>>((resolve, reject) => {
   this[withStartWorkflowOperationResolve] = resolve;
   this[withStartWorkflowOperationReject] = reject;
 });
+// Prevent unhandled rejection if executeUpdateWithStart fails before any response is
+// received. The error already propagates via the executeUpdateWithStart promise itself.
+this.workflowHandlePromise.catch(() => undefined);
```

Callers who explicitly `await startOp.workflowHandle()` will still observe the rejection, because the no-op `.catch()` creates a derived promise that discards the error — the original `workflowHandlePromise` is still rejected.

### Workaround (until fixed)

Attach `.catch()` to `startOp.workflowHandle()` before calling `executeUpdateWithStart`:

```ts
const startOp = new WithStartWorkflowOperation(queueWorkflow, { ... });
startOp.workflowHandle().catch(() => undefined); // suppress potential unhandled rejection
await client.workflow.executeUpdateWithStart(enqueueItem, {
  startWorkflowOperation: startOp,
  ...
});
```

### Environment/Versions

- SDK: `@temporalio/client` 1.15.0 (latest) — also confirmed on 1.14.1
- Server: Temporal 1.30.1 / CLI 1.6.1 (embedded via `@temporalio/testing`)
- Node.js: 22
- OS: macOS Darwin 25.3.0 (M-series)
